subject: FluxBank: sudden spike in latency & 5xx — dedicated pool saturation
messages:
From: Anu Patel <anu.patel@fluxbank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: production errors — urgent

Marissa —

We started seeing a spike in latency and an increasing rate of 5xx responses against our production service around 06:05 PT. Our SREs report token queues growing and some timeouts on downstream calls to your inference endpoint. We are seeing 2–6x tail-latency and ~8% 5xx in the last hour. This is impacting transaction confirmations for customers.

Attached is a very small sample of the request/response headers and timestamps (fluxbank_error_snippet.txt). Can you confirm whether this is a FluxBank-specific routing issue or a broader capacity problem on your side? We need an immediate mitigation plan; please treat as P1.

— Anu
Site Reliability Lead, FluxBank
ops@fluxbank.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Anu Patel <anu.patel@fluxbank.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 08:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: production errors — urgent

Anu — thanks for the flag and the snippet. I’m opening an ops bridge now and looping in our eng leads (Jonas, Rishi).

Immediate asks from our side:
- Can your team confirm whether traffic to your routed model (model: redwood-r14-dedicated) has any recent config changes (prompt injection, long-context workloads)?
- Can you provide a representative request ID for a 5xx you can share?

Planned immediate mitigations (subject to your OK):
1) Enable emergency burst from your reserved allocation for the next 3 hours to absorb current load.
2) If you approve, we can route non-critical routes to a hosted-compatible variant (redwood-r14-hosted-compat) while we drain the queue. Latency hit for some infrequent endpoints is expected but overall error rate should drop.
3) Our engineers will temporarily raise the pool headroom where possible; I’ve requested a slot insertion from Eng and asked Rishi for ETA.

I’ve attached initial triage notes (marissa_triage_notes.pdf) with the timeline we’re seeing. Please reply with a quick YES to the burst and switchover so we can execute.

— Marissa
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: production errors — urgent

Quick internal triage:
- Observed: dedicated-GPU pool assigned to FluxBank (pool id: pool-flx-7) shows sustained GPU utilization at 96–100% since ~05:50 PT. KV cache hit rate dropped and token queues per worker are >2x baseline.
- Impact: in-flight requests are being queued on the head node; our per-token latency kernel selection is falling back to a slower path for long-context requests, producing the tail-latency and 5xxs.

Short-term actions I can take immediately (with approvals):
A) Emergency burst: allocate 2 additional GPUs to pool-flx-7 for 3 hours (requires ops + procurement approval for overage credit); this should cut queue depth by ~40% in synthetic tests.
B) Route non-critical endpoints to a hosted-compat model (marissa has outbound permission) — this reduces load on pool by segregating traffic.
C) Increase KV cache TTL for repeated request prefixes (low-risk).

I’ve attached a quick dashboard snapshot and a link to the pool metrics: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/pool/fluxbank-123

If procurement/credit cannot be authorized quickly, we need to proceed with (B)+(C) and throttling for non-essential flows.

— Jonas
Sr. Prod Eng, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: production errors — urgent

I’m on the bridge. Quick technical note / plan:
- Root cause: sudden workload pattern shift (large batch prompt and long-context tokens) from one FluxBank route triggered a kernel selection path that is CPU-fallback heavy and causes worker thrash in the dedicated pool.
- Plan (ordered):
  1) Canary move non-critical route(s) to hosted-compat model (5–10% of traffic) to validate behavior (10m).
  2) If canary OK, flip 60% of non-critical traffic (20m).
  3) Insert 2 spare GPUs into pool-flx-7 (ETA 18m) — requires ops approval to hit overage path.
  4) Reconfigure aggressive KV caching and raise batching threshold for the pool (immediate after step 1).

I’ve uploaded the engineer runbook we’ll follow (engineer_runbook.md) and added a short checklist on rollback conditions. If procurement/credit will delay, we should start the canary now — it will reduce errors while we await capacity.

— Rishi
Eng Lead, Serving Runtime
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Anu Patel <anu.patel@fluxbank.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 12:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: production errors — urgent

Anu — summary & ask: thanks for your patience.

What we will do now (pending your approval):
- Start a 10m canary re-route of non-critical endpoints to hosted-compat (expected immediate drop in 5xx).
- If canary passes, we’ll expand and simultaneously turn on KV cache TTL increases.
- We’ll insert 2 GPUs to pool-flx-7 (if Naomi approves emergency overage).

Operational impact you should expect: small latency bump on the non-critical endpoints moved to hosted-compat (~20–50ms increase) but a meaningful reduction in error rate and queueing. Our goal is to restore 95th percentile to within SLA within 1 hour.

Please reply with YES to the burst & switchover, or let us know if you prefer we only do the canary.

Anu & team — I’m sorry for the impact here. I authorize an emergency burst of 2 GPUs to pool-flx-7 for up to 3 hours and we’ll absorb the overage on Redwood’s side up to the agreed one-time emergency credit cap in FLX-2025-86. 1) Please commit to a postmortem by EOW with root cause, timeline, and remediation (include kernel-selection telemetry and request shape that triggered the fallback). Use the postmortem template: https://drive.redwood.ai/s/FLX-2025-86/postmortem-template
2) Prepare an SLA impact slide for FluxBank (sla_impact_slide.pdf) so we can include the credit justification.

Anu — we’ll message you when the canary completes and before we execute the full switchover.
